CHAPTER VII
IRREVERSIBLE AND IRRETRIEVABLE
COMMITMENT OF RESOURCES
Irreversible commitment of resources relates to permanent effects which will persist beyond the life of the operation. Irretrievable commitments are those which will be invested or foregone as a result of the project.
The major commitment of resources is approximately 1,200,000,000 tons of coal from Tracts II and III. This production loss represents an estimated 1.7 percent of the subbituminous reserves within Montana and 2.8 percent of the strippable coal in Eastern Montana. 1/ It is estimated that approximately 17-22% of the Crow Tribes strippable coal reserves will be committed. This commitment of a non-renewable resource for income will offer an opportunity to improve the way of life, but will forego an opportunity for later resource development.
The use of an indeterminable amount of gravel, sand and clinker for a possible railroad loop, access roads and mine facilities will occur. Clinker deposits mined with overburden and moved with other spoils will also be irretrievably lost.
Coal mining and reclamation activities involved in the mining of each 1 million tons of coal will require 150,000 gallons of diesel fuel, gasoline, lubricants, 5,250,000 kwh of electrical power, explosives, and structural materials for building construction.
